The invariant (suffix-only, cache-monotonic compression) is now enforced by tests/test_cache_contract.py.

entries.claim: Measured on the live path since 1.45: an identical 10-turn agent conversation costs 60% less through distil than direct, checked against the provider's own reported cache_read. index.html also carries a rounded '83%' certified-savings stat tile.
entries.check_reason: A single live session on the maintainer's machine with no committed artifact; the 83% tile is a rounding of v-proof-rollup's 83.2%.
entries.note: Flagged rather than removed: the mechanism is documented, the specific session is not.

entries.claim: Distribution-free Learn-Then-Test / Hoeffding-Bentkus bound (same engine as E2): with 95% confidence the gated compressor costs a solvable task on <=11.4% of exchangeable runs, proven out-of-sample. The page also states the certified lossless ceiling at ~58% and distil-causal at ~81% on the 64-trajectory offline corpus.
entries.check_reason: The 11.4% bound is computed by the conformal module at report time rather than read from a committed file; the 58%/81% figures are the offline standings rounded (u-benchmark-offline-standings).
entries.note: distil/conformal.py implements the bound; there is no committed run to diff against.

entries.claim: Compression latency 0.026 ms/turn against LLMLingua-2's ~1,480 ms and Headroom 0.27.0's ~26 ms on the same live corpus, stated as ~1,000x faster than the nearest tool. On the 2026-06-23 codebench block the gap reads ~175x against llmlingua's 173.69 ms/turn.
entries.note: Ratio of the latency columns in the same 2026-07-05 run that backs v-proof-rollup; the 175x is from the 2026-09-04 codebench table (s-benchmark-headline), where llmlingua runs 173.69 ms against distil's ~1 ms.
entries.check_reason: a ratio of two latency columns rather than a figure the log prints; the columns themselves are in docs/paper/results/derc_live_compare.2026-07-05.log and the 2026-09-04 codebench output

entries.claim: Output shaping defaults to --shape-output auto on a metered session and is ON only when all three hold: the paired decision-equivalence verdict is at or above the shared reporting floor (50 A/B + 30 A/A), its harm bound (lower end of the paired difference interval) is inside the pre-registered +/-2pp certification margin, and the shadow output-token delta excludes zero on the saving side over at least 50 priced samples. Otherwise OFF with a stated reason. Turn-on evidence comes only from shadow rows tagged levers.shape == off, so shaped rows cannot keep shaping on; shaped rows at or above the floor whose harm bound is outside the budget turn it off; both sets are read over the last 7 days. Always off on subscription/OAuth. The last published live sample (398 A/B, 399 A/A) predates the lever tag and counts as zero rows; its harm bound (-4.5pp) is outside the 2pp budget regardless, so auto resolves to OFF.
entries.note: Mechanism is resolve_shape_output; the live-sample figures are from benchmarks/results/shadow-live-2026-09-15.json. The rule is covered by the decision matrix in tests/test_output.py; the thresholds are read from shadow.VERDICT_MIN_AB/VERDICT_MIN_AA and certify.gate.CERT_MARGIN (via output.SHAPE_HARM_MARGIN), not re-declared. Reply LENGTH cannot be measured offline (the deterministic oracle decides from blocks and emits no prose), so there is no corpus number for shaping and none is claimed: the n=6 output_pairs.jsonl A/B is a hand-written mechanism check, already labelled illustrative on the page. The README paragraph in the savings section restates this entry and originates no fact of its own.

entries.claim: On the maintainer's own Claude Code traffic (13,191 priced requests, 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-24, all in digest mode), distil saved an estimated 10.2% of the counterfactual bill: $286 saved against $2,510 billed, with cache reads and writes priced at list rates.
